title: Welcome to the Insane Clown Party
author: David Azerrad
content:
![Welcome to the Insane Clown
Party](https://storage.ghost.io/c/65/af/65afbdb5-30bf-4286-acc4-9535069adb42/content/images/2026/08/Screenshot-2026-08-04-at-7.37.51
---AM.png)

> _Whitepill: The Online Right and the Making of Trump 's America_  
> By Scott Greer  
> Passage, 300 pages, $34.95

There was a time, not too long ago, when the great threat to the right came
from its left flank. The conservative movement was filled with people who
eagerly canceled their own for transgressing liberal pieties. We all remember
the number of prominent conservatives who willingly bent the knee during the
BLM hysteria.

Ten years into the Trump era, it is no longer necessary to argue [_against
David French-ism_](https://firstthings.com/against-david-french-
ism/?ref=compactmag.com). The kids are far too based for that. Today, the task
is to argue against Tucker Carlson-ism, Nick Fuentes-ism, Candace Owens-ism,
and other forms of conspiratorial thinking that make it hard to love and
believe in America.

The kids, however, should not be berated by humorless scolds and told to read
Hayek and Kirk. Mainstream conservatism bores them and moral indignation
doesn't work when being transgressive is part of the point. I doubt Fuentes
knows much about Soviet communism, but it was clear how much he enjoyed
telling Tucker he was a fan of Joseph Stalin.

If the Millennials and Zoomers are to be rescued from the lunacy of much of
the online right, it must be done by someone who appreciates its contributions
but also recognizes its limitations. In _Whitepill: The Online Right and the
Making of Trump 's America_, Scott Greer offers a friendly and at times
compelling critique of the online right. Greer's credibility comes from the
fact that he hails from this world: He was canceled in 2018 after _The
Atlantic_ revealed he had edited and written for Richard Spencer's racialist
journal _Radix_. Greer has said that his writings from that time no longer
reflect his views, and he tracks the evolution of his thinking in his new
book.
